card.title: Why new things stop feeling new

body.claim: We tend to drift back toward a baseline level of happiness, though not completely.
body.why: The hedonic treadmill is the tendency to keep a fairly stable baseline of happiness despite external events. In a 1978 study of 22 lottery winners and 29 paraplegics, the lottery winners reported being similarly happy before and after winning. Later large panel studies found that divorce, a spouse's death, unemployment and disability do change long-term well-being, even though some adaptation occurs.

probes.question: What did the lottery winners in the 1978 study report?
options: Being similarly happy before and after

probes.question: True or false: large panel studies found that people fully adapt to every life event.
